epidemiology: Affects 17-44% of women with pelvic endometriosis. Predominantly seen in reproductive-age women (25-45 years).
pathophysiology: Pseudocyst formed by invagination and cyclic bleeding of ectopic endometrial tissue within the ovarian cortex, resulting in accumulated thick hemolyzed blood (chocolate fluid).

classic_ultrasound_features.feature_1: Homogeneous ground-glass internal echoes (diffuse low-level echogenicity throughout the cavity).
classic_ultrasound_features.feature_2: Unilocular or bilocular cyst with smooth thin wall (≤ 3 mm).
classic_ultrasound_features.feature_3: Wall echogenic foci / cholesterol deposits in the cyst wall (hyperechoic punctate foci without shadowing).
classic_ultrasound_features.feature_4: Kissing Ovaries Sign: Bilateral endometriomas adherent to each other behind the uterus in the pouch of Douglas, indicative of severe deep infiltrating endometriosis.

doppler_characteristics: Avascular cavity (Color Score 1). Mild peripheral wall flow may be seen, but internal flow is absent in typical benign endometriomas.
orads_category: O-RADS 2 (Risk < 1% for classic unilocular endometrioma < 10 cm in premenopausal women). O-RADS 3 if ≥ 10 cm.
malignant_transformation_risk: 0.5% - 1.0% risk of transformation into Clear Cell Carcinoma or Endometrioid Carcinoma, typically heralded by development of vascularized mural papillary projections or rapid size increase in women > 45 years.
differential_diagnosis: Hemorrhagic corpus luteum (distinguished by lacy reticular strands and spontaneous resolution within 6-8 weeks).
Mucinous cystadenoma (larger, multilocular with heterogeneous locules).
Pelvic abscess / Tubo-ovarian abscess (thickened irregular wall, fluid-debris level, hypervascularity on Doppler, positive sliding sign pain/tenderness).
management: Conservative medical therapy (oral contraceptives, dienogest) or laparoscopic cystectomy if symptomatic (dysmenorrhea, infertility, pelvic pain) or diameter > 4-5 cm.
